Laboratory cohorts of Trinidadian guppy (LP Yarra91) (Poecilia reticulata LP Yar91) reared under controlled thermal conditions at 26 °C [T = 26 °C] exhibit a maximum standard length of 3.65 cm [Li = 3.65 cm], a value consistent with the upper size limit reported for this strain in captive populations. This asymptotic body size, measured from the snout to the hypural plate, reflects the interplay between genetic constraints and the energetic demands of continuous growth in a stable environment. Compared to wild-caught individuals from the Yarra River system, which often remain smaller due to predation pressure, these laboratory-reared specimens achieve a more complete expression of their growth potential.

When provided with a high ration diet at 26 °C [T = 26 °C], females give birth after a gestation period of 26.75 days [ab = 26.75 days], a relatively rapid developmental duration that underscores the ability of this population to accelerate offspring production under resource-rich conditions. This abbreviated brooding interval, observed in multiparous females over successive litters, likely maximizes lifetime reproductive output by shortening the inter-brood interval.

In contrast, siblings assigned to a low-food regime at the same stable temperature of 26 °C [T = 26 °C] experienced a notably protracted gestation, with a mean age at birth of 27.5909091 days [ab = 27.5909091 days]. The difference of nearly one day compared to their well-fed counterparts illustrates the sensitivity of embryonic development to maternal nutritional state, a phenomenon well documented in poeciliid fishes. This delay may allow for more complete yolk utilization by the developing offspring.

The prolonged gestation under restricted rations likely results in offspring that are slightly larger or more developed at parturition, a trade-off that could confer a survival advantage in environments where food is chronically scarce. Such plasticity in gestation length is a key feature of the LP Yarra91 lineage and is consistent with the bet-hedging strategies observed in other Trinidadian guppy populations inhabiting variable streams. The 26 °C [T = 26 °C] baseline temperature used in these trials represents the optimal midpoint for this tropical species.

Beyond these reproductive metrics, the LP Yarra91 strain displays a typical Poecilia reticulata body plan, with pronounced sexual dimorphism evident in adult coloration and fin morphology. Males mature earlier and at a smaller size, while females continue to invest in somatic growth throughout their reproductive lifespan. Field surveys of the source population in the Yarra River catchment have noted a modal standard length of approximately 2.8 cm, suggesting that the maximum standard length of 3.65 cm [Li = 3.65 cm] achieved in the laboratory represents an upper boundary rarely attained under natural ecological constraints at a temperature of 26 °C [T = 26 °C].
